1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ("Cr.P.C") has been filed by the petitioners praying for quashing of FIR bearing no. 198/2020 registered at Police Station Mansarovar Park, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC") and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Issue notice.
Mr. Satish Kumar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
5. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Sudhir Kumar Ojha and Investigating Officer (IO) from Police Station Mansarovar Park, Delhi.

6. Brief facts of the present case are that on 21.02.2018, the petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 were married to each other as per the Hindu rites and customs and out of this wedlock, one child namely Vashishta was born on 13.03.2019.

On the complaint of complainant, an FIR bearing no.
198/2020 for the offence punishable under Section 498A/406/34 IPC was registered at Police Station Mansarovar Park against the petitioners.

It is stated that during the pendency of the case,

the disputes between the parties stands settled before counselling Cell, East District, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi on 23.03.2022.
7.
It is, however, stated that inadvertently, it is mentioned in the list of dates and events that the parties have got decree of divorce dated 09.12.2017.
The same be deemed to be deleted as inadvertently mentioned since the parties are staying together since 15.12.2021.

8. On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled/compromised between them and they have been living together since 15.12.2021 along with the minor child.
Respondent no. 2 further stated that she has no objection if FIR may be quashed.

9. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

10. Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 198/2020 registered at Police Station Mansarovar Park for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
11. The present petition stands disposed of.
12. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J JANUARY 19, 2023/
